clue.text: Study of arms hardly embracing the Queen? Hardly

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it, as arms embrace someone
the closing exclamation of doubt, as if the arrangement could hardly be right, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: taken as written, the word itself is the fodder
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that the study of coats of arms could ever really take in the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two different things: first it is the fodder, then, followed by a doubtful question mark, it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry is the formal study and design of coats of arms and armorial bearings.

clue.text: Get back small change from the Queen in 6

indicators.note: a small change of order to the letters, not loose coins, signals a rearrangement

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen and also a city in Canada, the 6 entry

explanation.surface: Someone recovers a few coins from the monarch while in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' looks like loose coins but tells us to rearrange REGINA, the Saskatchewan capital whose name means queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover or get it back after losing it.

clue.text: To devastate is, sadly, always part of the test

indicators.note: something gone wrong sadly suggests the letters of the next word are mixed up
only a fragment of the following words is taken, here two letters straddling them

explanation.surface: Someone laments that every exam ends in ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ALWAYS into LAYWAS; 'part of' takes TE from the run of letters in 'the test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay waste a place is to ravage or devastate it completely.

clue.text: Worm eaten plate in Veronese's name

indicators.note: the plate's letter is placed inside the painter's first name

parts.note: the Renaissance painter was Paolo Veronese
an L-plate is the learner's sign on a British car, so plate gives L

explanation.surface: A painting by Veronese shows a dish that worms have got into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worm eaten' looks like decay, but the definition is a worm that people eat; an L-plate is the red L shown by British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The palolo is a Pacific marine worm whose spawning swarms are gathered and eaten as a delicacy in Samoa.

clue.text: 6's turn — turn "bee" into "silk"

definitions.note: the possessive stands for a province belonging to Canada, the 6 entry

indicators.note: the turned letters are put inside the abbreviation for silk

parts.note: a QC, Queen's Counsel, is said to take silk, so silk gives QC
a U-turn, so turn gives the letter U

indicators.note: to turn the word bee is to rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to change a bee into silk, apparently Canada's go.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'turn' gives U and the second turns BEE into EBE; 'into' puts both inside QC. QC is also the province's postal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-speaking region is one of the provinces of Canada, the 6 entry.

clue.text: Distant object as wrong as right

parts.note: qua means as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: the next word is set wrong, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: Something far off is as mistaken as it is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns the second AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A quasar is an extremely remote, very luminous astronomical object.

clue.text: With last part of 1 11?

parts.note: the last three letters of the heraldry entry at 1 follow this word in a ginger ale brand name, just as they precede the 11 entry in a phrase for terra firma; so this is a land that goes with that word

explanation.surface: A puzzle about adding the end of one entry to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The last part of HERALDRY is DRY: put after this answer it names a ginger ale, and before 11 it means solid ground, so the answer is a land that pairs with DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country, that is a land, and the brand of ginger ale bears its name followed by that word.

clue.text: First loose broadcaster?

parts.note: A is first in the alphabet and grade A is first-class
to loose is to untie

explanation.surface: Something gets set free before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is a long-standing affectionate nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.

clue.text: A winter in France going topless? A joke everywhere

indicators.note: losing the top means the first letter of the French winter word is dropped

parts.note: French for a winter is un hiver
a sally is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A French winter spent without tops is a joke all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the H of HIVER, leaving UN IVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done universally is done in every place, by all.

clue.text: Confession of a gadabout and globetrotter?

definitions.text: Confession of a gadabout and globetrotter?

parts.words: Confession of a gadabout and globetrotter?
parts.note: read backwards, the explorer's name spells out an admission that one is a gad, so gad about the name to get the confession

explanation.surface: A wandering traveller owns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Vasco da Gama, the Portuguese explorer, was a true globetrotter; backwards his surname reads AM A GAD, which is what a gadabout would confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who first sailed from Europe to India round Africa.

clue.text: Old nun wed fan shock in 6

definitions.note: it is a place in Canada, the 6 entry

indicators.note: a shock throws things into disorder, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: an elderly nun marries a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' reads like a headline, but it signals an anagram of OLD NUN WED FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This island province on the Atlantic coast lies in Canada, along with Labrador.

clue.text: See 10
6's, not 25, one including 9

parts.note: a province of Canada that is not an island but whose name, read through, contains the first name of the explorer at 9

explanation.surface: A riddle of cross-references about a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a peninsula, not an island like its neighbours, and its letters contain VASCO, the first name of 9 (da Gama).
explanation.definitionFit: This Maritime province of Canada is a mainland peninsula whose name means New Scotland.

clue.text: Make leaderless Navy obey rule, if you don't mind

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to form a new word from them
the first letter of the word is removed, as an army loses its leader

explanation.surface: An order to make a headless navy follow regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops N from NAVY to leave AVY; 'Make' rearranges AVY with OBEY and RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: This polite formula asks permission, much as one says 'with your permission'.

clue.text: Ladies of a certain age adore LSD trips

indicators.note: LSD trips, but also a stumble that throws letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Older women who love acid-induced hallucinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' fits the drug picture but signals an anagram of ADORE LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Old dears is a fond British phrase for elderly ladies.

clue.text: Revised criticism with calf binding is standing up

indicators.note: the meat wraps round the other piece, as a cover binds a book

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf

indicators.note: when a text is revised its parts are reordered

parts.note: a crit is an informal word for a critique or criticism

explanation.surface: A critique revised in a calfskin binding is standing upright.
explanation.walkthrough: Calf binding suggests leather bookbinding, but here calf is the meat; 'Revised' and 'binding' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vertical is upright, standing straight up.

clue.text: Ask a person to leave

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
one can mean a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a definition of the whole, but splits into ask and a person; the answer is an order meaning leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic command is an order to go away, the imperative of leaving.

clue.text: Quiet piece of cloth in tartan

indicators.note: the small piece goes inside the patterned fabric

parts.note: plaid is checked tartan cloth

indicators.note: only a piece of the word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A small scrap of fabric is set into a tartan design, calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' takes C from cloth, and 'in' puts it into PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A placid person is calm and quiet, not easily upset.

clue.text: Watch revolver obtained from another

definitions.meaning: the pointer that sweeps round a watch face each minute
owned before by someone else, used

explanation.surface: A watch's ticking pointer, bought from a previous owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The fast hand on a watch circles once a minute; used goods are described with the same hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: A power circuit, perhaps, raised in 6

definitions.note: it is a city in Canada, the 6 entry

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the pieces are turned backwards

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power
a circuit is a ring, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Perhaps an electrical circuit was put up in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses A WATT O in this down clue; the city is Canada's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, in Ontario.

clue.text: Put down flower without concession arising

indicators.note: here without means outside, so the river surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means going up, read backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone

explanation.surface: A bloom is laid down without any giving way.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means something that flows, a river, not a bloom; 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove or put them down from power.

clue.text: Part of word given by orphan?

indicators.note: an orphan has no parent, so the father, pa, is taken away

parts.note: parole is a word given, a promise of good conduct

explanation.surface: A child without parents speaks a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orphan' removes PA (father) from PAROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a part played by an actor.

clue.text: 6's torn off during dinner?

definitions.note: the possessive stands for a city belonging to Canada, the 6 entry

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other, so its letters go inside

parts.note: dinner is a meal

indicators.note: something gone off is spoilt or wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Something of Canada's is ripped away while people eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn off' looks like part of the picture, but 'off' is the anagram signal and the city is the definition by way of 6's.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreal is the largest city of Quebec, a Canadian city.
